bm25.title: Children and SARS-CoV-2 infection: innocent bystanders…until proven otherwise
bm25.text: Children and SARS-CoV-2 infection: innocent bystanders…until proven otherwise In this commentary, we focus our attention on what is known about SARS-CoV-2 infection in the pediatric population. We report literature and National data. The possible and different explanations for understanding why the infection seems to be more benign and less frequent in children are discussed. The possible role of children in the COVID-19 viral disease pandemic is also commented. Finally, our work suggests to search for future evidence and containment strategies to manage virus spread.

dense.title: Development of a Synthetic Poxvirus-Based SARS-CoV-2 Vaccine
dense.text: Development of a Synthetic Poxvirus-Based SARS-CoV-2 Vaccine Modified Vaccinia Ankara (MVA) is a highly attenuated poxvirus vector that is widely used to develop vaccines for infectious diseases and cancer. We developed a novel vaccine platform based on a unique three-plasmid system to efficiently generate recombinant MVA vectors from chemically synthesized DNA. In response to the ongoing global pandemic caused by SARS coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2), we used this novel vaccine platform to rapidly produce fully synthetic MVA (sMVA) vectors co-expressing SARS-CoV-2 spike and nucleocapsid antigens, two immunodominant antigens implicated in protective immunity. Mice immunized with these sMVA vectors developed robust SARS-CoV-2 antigen-specific humoral and cellular immune responses, including potent neutralizing antibodies. These results demonstrate the potential of a novel vaccine platform based on synthetic DNA to efficiently generate recombinant MVA vectors and to rapidly develop a multi-antigenic poxvirus-based SARS-CoV-2 vaccine candidate.

dense.title: Replication-competent vesicular stomatitis virus vaccine vector protects against SARS-CoV-2-mediated pathogenesis
dense.text: Replication-competent vesicular stomatitis virus vaccine vector protects against SARS-CoV-2-mediated pathogenesis Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has caused millions of human infections and hundreds of thousands of deaths. Accordingly, an effective vaccine is of critical importance in mitigating coronavirus induced disease 2019 (COVID-19) and curtailing the pandemic. We developed a replication-competent vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV)-based vaccine by introducing a modified form of the SARS-CoV-2 spike gene in place of the native glycoprotein gene (VSV-eGFP-SARS-CoV-2). Immunization of mice with VSV-eGFP-SARS-CoV-2 elicits high titers of antibodies that neutralize SARS-CoV-2 infection and target the receptor binding domain that engages human angiotensin converting enzyme-2 (ACE2). Upon challenge with a human isolate of SARS-CoV-2, mice expressing human ACE2 and immunized with VSV-eGFP-SARS-CoV-2 show profoundly reduced viral infection and inflammation in the lung indicating protection against pneumonia. Finally, passive transfer of sera from VSV-eGFP-SARS-CoV-2-immunized animals protects naïve mice from SARS-CoV-2 challenge. These data support development of VSV-eGFP-SARS-CoV-2 as an attenuated, replication-competent vaccine against SARS-CoV-2.

dense.title: Immunoinformatics-guided designing of epitope-based subunit vaccine against the SARS Coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2)
dense.text: Immunoinformatics-guided designing of epitope-based subunit vaccine against the SARS Coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2) SARS Coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2) pandemic has become a global issue which has raised the concern of scientific community to design and discover a counter-measure against this deadly virus which has caused deaths of numerous infected people upon infection and spreading. To date, no effective vaccine is available which can combat the infection caused by this virus. This study was conducted to design possible epitope-based subunit vaccines against the SARS-CoV-2 virus using the approaches of reverse vaccinology and immunoinformatics. Upon continual computational experimentation three possible vaccine constructs were designed and one vaccine construct was selected as the best vaccine based on molecular docking study which is supposed to effectively act against SARS-CoV-2. Thereafter, molecular dynamics simulation and in silico codon adaptation experiments were carried out in order to check biological stability and find effective mass production strategy of the selected vaccine. This study should contribute to uphold the present efforts of the researches to secure a definitive treatment for this lethal disease.

dense.title: The promise of mRNA vaccines: a biotech and industrial perspective
dense.text: The promise of mRNA vaccines: a biotech and industrial perspective mRNA technologies have the potential to transform areas of medicine, including the prophylaxis of infectious diseases. The advantages for vaccines range from the acceleration of immunogen discovery to rapid response and multiple disease target manufacturing. A greater understanding of quality attributes that dictate translation efficiency, as well as a comprehensive appreciation of the importance of mRNA delivery, are influencing a new era of investment in development activities. The application of translational sciences and growing early-phase clinical experience continue to inform candidate vaccine selection. Here we review the state of the art for the prevention of infectious diseases by using mRNA and pertinent topics to the biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries.

aiml.title: Attention Is All You Need
aiml.text: Attention Is All You Need. The Transformer architecture, based solely on attention mechanisms without recurrence or convolutions, achieves superior results on machine translation. Self-attention allows each position in the encoder to attend to all positions in the encoder. Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions. The Transformer achieves 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German translation.

aiml.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention
aiml.text: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention. FlashAttention is an IO-aware exact attention algorithm that uses tiling to reduce memory reads and writes between GPU HBM and on-chip SRAM. FlashAttention trains Transformers 2-4x faster than baselines and uses 5-20x less memory with no approximation. It makes exact attention feasible on sequences of 64K tokens on a single A100 GPU.

aiml.title: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer
aiml.text: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer. Longformer uses a combination of windowed local-context self-attention and global attention that scales linearly with sequence length, making it easy to process documents of thousands of tokens. It achieves state-of-the-art results on character-level language modeling and several long document NLP tasks.

aiml.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers
aiml.text: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers. BERT pre-trains deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers using Masked Language Modeling and Next Sentence Prediction. Fine-tuned BERT achieves state-of-the-art on eleven NLP tasks including SQuAD and GLUE.

aiml.title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
aiml.text: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach. RoBERTa shows BERT was significantly undertrained. Key improvements include training longer with bigger batches on more data, removing Next Sentence Prediction, training on longer sequences, and dynamically changing masking patterns. RoBERTa matches or exceeds XLNet on all benchmarks.

aiml.title: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning
aiml.text: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning. ALBERT uses factorized embedding parameterization and cross-layer parameter sharing to reduce memory consumption and increase BERT training speed. ALBERT achieves state-of-the-art results on GLUE, RACE, and SQuAD benchmarks while using 18x fewer parameters than BERT-large.

aiml.title: DistilBERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter
aiml.text: DistilBERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter. DistilBERT is trained by distilling BERT base using knowledge distillation during pretraining. It has 40% fewer parameters, runs 60% faster, and retains 97% of BERT's language understanding capabilities and 60% faster.

aiml.title: XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining
aiml.text: XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining. XLNet is a generalized autoregressive pretraining method that enables learning bidirectional contexts by maximizing the expected likelihood over all permutations of the factorization order during training. XLNet outperforms BERT on 20 tasks including SQuAD 2.0, NaturalQuestions, GLUE.

aiml.title: GPT-2: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
aiml.text: GPT-2: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners. GPT-2 with 1.5B parameters demonstrates that language models begin to learn NLP tasks without explicit supervision when trained on WebText, 8 million web pages. The model achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on 7 out of 8 tested language modeling datasets.

aiml.title: GPT-3: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
aiml.text: GPT-3: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners. GPT-3 with 175B parameters achieves strong few-shot performance on many NLP tasks, sometimes rivaling fine-tuned models. In-context learning with just a few examples enables strong results on translation, question-answering, cloze tasks, and several tasks requiring on-the-fly reasoning.

aiml.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
aiml.text: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models. LLaMA models from 7B to 65B parameters are trained on publicly available data only. LLaMA-13B outperforms GPT-3 on most benchmarks despite being 10x smaller. LLaMA-65B is competitive with Chinchilla-70B and PaLM-540B.

aiml.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
aiml.text: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models. Llama 2 pretrained and fine-tuned LLMs from 7B to 70B parameters. Llama 2-Chat is optimized for dialogue using RLHF with over 1 million human annotations. Llama 2-Chat outperforms open-source chat models and is on par with some closed-source models on human evaluations.

aiml.title: Mistral 7B
aiml.text: Mistral 7B. Mistral 7B outperforms Llama 2 13B on all benchmarks and Llama 1 34B on many benchmarks. It uses grouped-query attention for faster inference and sliding window attention to handle sequences of arbitrary length with no memory overhead.

aiml.title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways
aiml.text: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways. PaLM is a 540B parameter dense decoder-only Transformer model trained using Pathways on 780B tokens. PaLM achieves breakthrough performance on 28 of 29 NLP tasks, demonstrates few-shot chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities, and shows exceptional multilingual performance.

aiml.title: Chinchilla: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
aiml.text: Chinchilla: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models. Chinchilla scaling laws show current LLMs are significantly undertrained. For compute-optimal training, model size and training tokens should be scaled equally. Chinchilla 70B trained on 1.4T tokens outperforms Gopher 280B, GPT-3 175B, and PaLM 540B despite using the same compute budget as Gopher.

aiml.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
aiml.text: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models. LoRA freezes pretrained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each Transformer layer. This reduces trainable parameters by 10000x and GPU memory by 3x compared to fine-tuning. LoRA matches or outperforms fine-tuning on GPT-3 and GPT-2 with no additional inference latency.

aiml.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
aiml.text: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs. QLoRA backpropagates gradients through a frozen 4-bit quantized pretrained LLM into Low Rank Adapters. QLoRA reduces memory enough to finetune a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU while preserving full 16-bit finetuning performance. The resulting Guanaco model outperforms previous openly released models on the Vicuna benchmark.

aiml.title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation
aiml.text: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation. Prefix-tuning prepends a sequence of continuous task-specific vectors to the input and keeps LM parameters frozen while optimizing only the prefix. Prefix-tuning with 0.1% of parameters matches fine-tuning on table-to-text and summarization in full-data settings and outperforms fine-tuning in low-data settings.

aiml.title: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning
aiml.text: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning. Prompt tuning conditions frozen language models with a small number of learned soft prompt tokens prepended to the input. At the scale of T5-XXL, prompt tuning matches the strong performance of model tuning while being much more parameter-efficient. Soft prompts are learned through backpropagation over a labeled training set.

aiml.title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for NLP
aiml.text: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for NLP. Adapters add small bottleneck layers to each transformer layer and only train these adapter layers during fine-tuning, keeping the pretrained model frozen. Adapters achieve near state-of-the-art performance on GLUE with only 3.6% additional parameters per task.

aiml.title: InstructGPT: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
aiml.text: InstructGPT: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback. InstructGPT fine-tunes GPT-3 with RLHF using a dataset of human-written demonstrations and comparisons. A reward model trained on human comparisons is used as the reward signal in PPO training. InstructGPT is preferred over GPT-3 by labelers despite having 100x fewer parameters.

aiml.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
aiml.text: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model. DPO shows that the RLHF objective can be optimized exactly with a simple cross-entropy loss on preference data without reward modeling or RL. DPO is more stable, computationally lighter, and produces similar or better performance compared to RLHF with PPO on summarization and dialogue.

aiml.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
aiml.text: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback. Constitutional AI trains harmless AI assistants through self-improvement using a list of principles called a constitution. The AI generates responses, critiques them according to the constitution, and revises them. The final RL step uses AI-generated feedback instead of human feedback labels.

aiml.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
aiml.text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks. RAG combines parametric memory from a pretrained seq2seq model with non-parametric memory from a dense passage retriever. The retriever finds relevant documents and the generator produces the final answer conditioned on both the input and retrieved documents. RAG achieves state-of-the-art on Open NQ, WebQ and CuratedTrec.

aiml.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
aiml.text: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering. DPR uses two independent BERT encoders for queries and passages and trains them with in-batch negative sampling. DPR outperforms BM25 by 9-19% exact match accuracy on NQ, TriviaQA, WebQ, and CuratedTrec, while being trained on only 1000 examples for some datasets.

aiml.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Late Interaction
aiml.text: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Late Interaction. ColBERT uses late interaction: independently encode query and document with BERT, then compute relevance via a cheap MaxSim operation over all token embeddings. ColBERT is 170x faster than BERT cross-encoder re-rankers while achieving comparable MRR@10 on MS MARCO.

aiml.title: Sparse, Dense, and Attentional Representations for Text Retrieval
aiml.text: Sparse, Dense, and Attentional Representations for Text Retrieval. Hybrid retrieval combining sparse BM25 and dense embeddings consistently outperforms either alone across diverse retrieval tasks. Linear interpolation of BM25 and dense scores with a fixed weight achieves strong performance. The paper motivates adaptive weighting per query.

aiml.title: Blended RAG: Improving RAG Accuracy with Semantic Search and Hybrid Query-Based Retrievers
aiml.text: Blended RAG: Improving RAG Accuracy with Semantic Search and Hybrid Query-Based Retrievers. Blended RAG combines BM25, KNN dense vectors, and ELSER sparse semantic encoder via hybrid query strategies (Best Fields, Cross Fields, Phrase Prefix). Blended RAG achieves NDCG@10=0.87 on TREC-COVID and 0.67 on NQ, outperforming all prior benchmarks including COCO-DR and monoT5-3B.

aiml.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
aiml.text: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection. Self-RAG trains an LLM to adaptively retrieve passages and generate text interleaved with special reflection tokens for retrieval, relevance, support and utility. Self-RAG outperforms ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-Chat on open-domain QA, reasoning, and fact verification.

aiml.title: HyDE: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
aiml.text: HyDE: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels. HyDE instructs an LLM to generate a hypothetical document for the query, then uses an encoder to embed this hypothetical document for retrieval. Despite being unreal, the hypothetical document captures relevance patterns and dramatically improves zero-shot dense retrieval performance.

aiml.title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval
aiml.text: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval. RAPTOR recursively embeds, clusters, and summarizes chunks of text building a tree with different levels of abstraction. At inference time it retrieves from this tree integrating information across lengthy documents at different levels. RAPTOR significantly outperforms chunk-based RAG on QASPER and NarrativeQA.

aiml.title: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented LLMs through Question Complexity
aiml.text: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented LLMs through Question Complexity. Adaptive-RAG trains a small classifier to predict query complexity and route queries to the appropriate retrieval strategy: no retrieval, single-step retrieval, or multi-step retrieval. This achieves better performance and efficiency than always using the most complex strategy.

aiml.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
aiml.text: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks. SBERT uses siamese and triplet network structures with BERT to produce fixed-size sentence embeddings. SBERT reduces the time for finding the most similar pair from 65 hours with BERT to 5 seconds while maintaining accuracy. SBERT sets new state-of-the-art on semantic textual similarity benchmarks.

aiml.title: BGE M3-Embedding: Multi-Lingual Multi-Functionality Multi-Granularity Text Embeddings
aiml.text: BGE M3-Embedding: Multi-Lingual Multi-Functionality Multi-Granularity Text Embeddings. M3-Embedding supports 100+ languages and unifies dense retrieval, lexical retrieval, and multi-vector retrieval in a single model trained with self-knowledge distillation. M3 achieves state-of-the-art on BEIR and MIRACL benchmarks.

aiml.title: E5: Text Embeddings by Weakly-Supervised Contrastive Pre-training
aiml.text: E5: Text Embeddings by Weakly-Supervised Contrastive Pre-training. E5 uses weakly supervised contrastive pretraining on curated web text pairs without expensive labeled data. E5 outperforms models trained on labeled datasets on both BEIR and MTEB benchmarks. Fine-tuned E5-large achieves the best overall performance on MTEB.

aiml.title: FAISS: Billion-scale similarity search with GPUs
aiml.text: FAISS: Billion-scale similarity search with GPUs. FAISS provides efficient similarity search for dense vectors including IndexFlatL2, IndexIVFFlat, and IndexHNSWFlat. GPU FAISS achieves billion-scale nearest-neighbor search in one second. FAISS is widely used in recommendation systems, visual search, and retrieval augmented generation pipelines.

aiml.title: HNSW: Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search
aiml.text: HNSW: Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search. HNSW builds a multilayer graph structure where each node is connected to its nearest neighbors at different scales. Search navigates from coarse to fine layers. HNSW outperforms all existing ANN methods on recall-performance tradeoff for all query scales.

aiml.title: BM25: The Probabilistic Relevance Framework
aiml.text: BM25: The Probabilistic Relevance Framework. BM25 ranks documents by the sum of IDF-weighted term frequency scores with saturation and document length normalization. BM25 is a strong baseline for information retrieval that consistently outperforms TF-IDF and is used as the default ranker in Elasticsearch and Lucene search engines.

aiml.title: SPLADE: Sparse Lexical and Expansion Model for First Stage Retrieval
aiml.text: SPLADE: Sparse Lexical and Expansion Model for First Stage Retrieval. SPLADE learns sparse representations by applying a log-saturation over BERT token representations with max-pooling, producing bag-of-words style sparse vectors. SPLADE achieves state-of-the-art retrieval on MS MARCO while matching BM25 efficiency through an inverted index.

aiml.title: SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text
aiml.text: SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text. SQuAD contains 100,000+ crowdsourced question-answer pairs on 500+ Wikipedia articles where answers are text spans. SQuAD v2 adds 50,000 unanswerable questions. SQuAD is the standard benchmark for reading comprehension and question answering research.

aiml.title: Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research
aiml.text: Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research. Natural Questions consists of 307,373 Google search queries paired with Wikipedia pages containing long and short answer annotations. NQ tests the ability to retrieve and read evidence from Wikipedia to answer naturally occurring questions.

aiml.title: HotpotQA: Multi-hop Question Answering
aiml.text: HotpotQA: Multi-hop Question Answering. HotpotQA contains 113K Wikipedia-based questions requiring multi-hop reasoning over multiple documents with supporting fact supervision. It tests two reasoning strategies: bridge questions requiring chaining two documents and comparison questions requiring comparing two entities.

aiml.title: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of IR Models
aiml.text: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of IR Models. BEIR contains 18 diverse retrieval datasets covering bio-medical, financial, scientific, and general domains. BM25 is a surprisingly strong baseline, outperforming many neural models in zero-shot settings, motivating domain-specific fine-tuning of retrieval models.

aiml.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
aiml.text: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models. Chain-of-thought prompting provides a series of intermediate reasoning steps as few-shot examples to elicit multi-step reasoning. CoT is an emergent ability appearing only in models above 100B parameters. CoT prompting significantly improves arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning.

aiml.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning
aiml.text: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning. Self-consistency samples a diverse set of reasoning paths and selects the most consistent final answer by majority voting. Self-consistency significantly improves CoT prompting performance on arithmetic and commonsense reasoning, outperforming greedy decoding by large margins.

aiml.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs
aiml.text: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs. Tree of Thoughts generalizes CoT to allow exploration of multiple reasoning paths, self-evaluation of intermediate thoughts, and lookahead or backtracking. ToT achieves 74% on Game of 24 where CoT achieves only 4%, and significantly improves creative writing.

aiml.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
aiml.text: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models. ReAct interleaves reasoning traces and task-specific actions, allowing the model to dynamically retrieve information and update its plan. ReAct outperforms chain-of-thought on HotpotQA and FEVER, and outperforms imitation and reinforcement learning on interactive decision tasks.

aiml.title: CLIP: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
aiml.text: CLIP: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision. CLIP trains a vision encoder and text encoder jointly to predict which caption matches which image using a contrastive objective on 400M image-text pairs. CLIP achieves zero-shot transfer competitive with supervised baselines on ImageNet and 30 other datasets.

aiml.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Vision Transformer
aiml.text: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Vision Transformer. ViT applies a standard Transformer to sequences of image patches for image classification. When pre-trained on large datasets, ViT attains excellent results on ImageNet, CIFAR-100, and VTAB while requiring substantially fewer computational resources than CNNs to train.

aiml.title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
aiml.text: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning. Flamingo bridges pretrained vision-only and language-only models with cross-attention layers. Flamingo achieves state-of-the-art few-shot performance on 16 multimodal benchmarks including VQA, COCO captioning, and video QA by conditioning on arbitrarily interleaved images and text.

aiml.title: LLaVA: Visual Instruction Tuning
aiml.text: LLaVA: Visual Instruction Tuning. LLaVA connects CLIP visual encoder with LLaMA using a simple linear projection and trains on GPT-4 generated multimodal instruction-following data. LLaVA-1.5 achieves state-of-the-art on 11 benchmarks using only public data.

aiml.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Survey
aiml.text: Knowledge Distillation: A Survey. Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from a large teacher model to a small student model through soft probability targets, intermediate feature matching, or attention transfer. Applications include model compression, cross-modal learning, and continual learning.

aiml.title: TinyBERT: Distilling BERT for NLU
aiml.text: TinyBERT: Distilling BERT for NLU. TinyBERT introduces transformer distillation with attention matrix distillation and value relation distillation. TinyBERT-4L has 7.5x fewer parameters and is 9.4x faster than BERT-base while achieving 96.8% of BERT performance on GLUE.

aiml.title: Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts
aiml.text: Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts. The Sparsely-Gated MoE layer routes each input to the top-k of N expert networks using a learnable gating network. MoE increases model capacity 1000x with only minor computational overhead by using sparse activation. MoE achieves state-of-the-art on WMT En-Fr translation.

aiml.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models
aiml.text: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models. Switch Transformer simplifies MoE by routing each token to exactly one expert. This reduces communication costs and achieves 7x faster pretraining speed than T5 at the same FLOP count. Switch Transformers scale to 1.6 trillion parameters.

aiml.title: Mixtral of Experts
aiml.text: Mixtral of Experts. Mixtral 8x7B uses 8 experts per MoE layer with top-2 routing, accessing only 13B active parameters out of 47B total. Mixtral matches or outperforms Llama 2 70B and GPT-3.5 on most benchmarks while being 6x faster at inference.

aiml.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
aiml.text: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models. Neural language model performance scales as power-laws with model size, dataset size, and compute budget, spanning 7 orders of magnitude. For a fixed compute budget, larger models trained on less data outperform smaller models trained longer. These laws inform optimal resource allocation.

aiml.title: Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models
aiml.text: Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models. Emergent abilities appear abruptly when model scale crosses certain thresholds, not present in smaller models. Examples include multi-step arithmetic, taking exams, and explaining jokes. Emergence motivates continued scaling of language models.

aiml.title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision
aiml.text: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision. FActScore breaks generated text into atomic facts and measures the percentage supported by a reliable knowledge source. FActScore better correlates with human factuality judgments than existing metrics. Current LLMs achieve only 58.4% FActScore on biography generation.

aiml.title: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods
aiml.text: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods. TruthfulQA contains 817 questions designed to elicit common misconceptions. GPT-3 is truthful on only 58% of questions while humans achieve 94%. Larger models tend to be less truthful, imitating falsehoods in pretraining data. RLHF substantially improves truthfulness.

aiml.title: Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation
aiml.text: Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation. Hallucination in NLG includes intrinsic contradictions of source content and extrinsic unverifiable claims. Key causes are exposure bias, copy mechanism errors, and parametric knowledge conflicts. Mitigation strategies include retrieval augmentation, constrained decoding, and RLHF.

aiml.title: YOLO: You Only Look Once: Unified Real-Time Object Detection
aiml.text: YOLO: You Only Look Once: Unified Real-Time Object Detection. YOLO frames object detection as regression to bounding boxes and class probabilities from a single neural network pass. YOLO processes images at 45 FPS with 63.4 mAP on PASCAL VOC, compared to 7 FPS for DPM and 18 FPS for Fast RCNN while achieving comparable accuracy.

aiml.title: DETR: End-to-End Object Detection with Transformers
aiml.text: DETR: End-to-End Object Detection with Transformers. DETR uses a Transformer encoder-decoder with bipartite matching loss to directly predict a set of object detections, eliminating NMS and anchor generation. DETR achieves 42.0 AP on COCO, matching Faster RCNN with fewer parameters and strong performance on large objects.

aiml.title: Graph Convolutional Networks for Semi-Supervised Classification
aiml.text: Graph Convolutional Networks for Semi-Supervised Classification. GCN propagates features through a graph using a simple layer-wise rule motivated by first-order spectral graph convolutions. GCN achieves state-of-the-art on semi-supervised node classification on Cora, Citeseer, and Pubmed citation networks with only a fraction of labeled nodes.

aiml.title: Graph Attention Networks
aiml.text: Graph Attention Networks. GAT computes node representations by attending over neighborhoods with learnable attention weights that do not require knowledge of the graph structure. GAT achieves state-of-the-art on Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed, and the inductive PPI dataset.

aiml.title: Codex: Evaluating LLMs Trained on Code
aiml.text: Codex: Evaluating LLMs Trained on Code. Codex is GPT fine-tuned on 100B tokens of public GitHub code. On HumanEval, a new benchmark of 164 Python programming problems, Codex solves 28.8% using a single sample and 70.2% using 100 samples. GPT-3 solves 0% on HumanEval.

aiml.title: CodeBERT: A Pre-Trained Model for Programming and Natural Languages
aiml.text: CodeBERT: A Pre-Trained Model for Programming and Natural Languages. CodeBERT is bimodal BERT pretrained on 8.35M code-documentation pairs from GitHub in 6 programming languages. CodeBERT achieves state-of-the-art on code search, code documentation generation, and code-to-code search tasks.

aiml.title: Neural Machine Translation with Subword Units (BPE)
aiml.text: Neural Machine Translation with Subword Units (BPE). Byte-pair encoding learns a variable-length subword vocabulary by iteratively merging the most frequent symbol pairs. BPE enables open-vocabulary NMT and reduces out-of-vocabulary rates. BPE improves BLEU by 1.1-11.8 on WMT translation tasks.

aiml.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models: A Survey
aiml.text: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models: A Survey. This survey covers additive methods (adapters, prefix tuning, prompt tuning), selective methods (BitFit, DiffPruning), reparameterization methods (LoRA, IA3), and hybrid methods. PEFT methods achieve comparable performance to full fine-tuning with 0.1-3% of parameters updated.

aiml.title: SimCLR: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning
aiml.text: SimCLR: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning. SimCLR applies contrastive loss to representations after a nonlinear projection head using augmentations including random cropping, color distortion, and Gaussian blur. SimCLR achieves 76.5% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet with ResNet-50, outperforming previous self-supervised methods by 7%.

aiml.title: FedAvg: Communication-Efficient Learning from Decentralized Data
aiml.text: FedAvg: Communication-Efficient Learning from Decentralized Data. FedAvg performs multiple local SGD steps on each client before averaging model weights on the server. FedAvg reduces communication rounds by 10-100x over synchronous SGD while achieving similar accuracy on image classification and language modeling tasks.

aiml.title: T5: Exploring Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
aiml.text: T5: Exploring Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer. T5 converts every NLP task into text-to-text format and pre-trains with a span-corruption objective on the Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus. T5-11B achieves state-of-the-art on GLUE, SuperGLUE, SQuAD, CNN-DM, and WMT translation benchmarks.

aiml.title: BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training
aiml.text: BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training. BART pre-trains a standard sequence-to-sequence Transformer by learning to reconstruct text from corrupted input using token masking, deletion, infilling, permutation and rotation. BART achieves state-of-the-art on summarization, dialogue, and abstractive QA.

aiml.title: Passage Re-ranking with BERT
aiml.text: Passage Re-ranking with BERT. Cross-encoder BERT re-ranker concatenates query and passage and fine-tunes on MS MARCO click labels. BERT re-ranker achieves MRR@10 of 0.365 on MS MARCO dev vs 0.167 for BM25. A two-stage BM25+BERT pipeline achieves 0.358 MRR@10 efficiently.

aiml.title: Query Rewriting for Retrieval-Augmented LLMs
aiml.text: Query Rewriting for Retrieval-Augmented LLMs. Rewrite-Retrieve-Read uses an LLM to rewrite user queries to be more specific before retrieval. The rewritten query leads to more relevant retrieved documents and better final answers. Query rewriting improves performance on open-domain QA by up to 12% accuracy.

aiml.title: FLARE: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
aiml.text: FLARE: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation. FLARE iteratively predicts upcoming sentences, retrieves if low-probability tokens appear, and regenerates with retrieved documents as context. FLARE outperforms standard RAG and RETRO on long-form generation tasks including open-domain QA and fact completion.

aiml.title: Graph RAG: Query-Focused Summarization over Document Corpora
aiml.text: Graph RAG: Query-Focused Summarization over Document Corpora. Graph RAG extracts an entity knowledge graph from source documents using an LLM, generates community summaries at multiple granularities, and answers queries by combining global and local context. Graph RAG significantly outperforms standard RAG on sensemaking queries.

aiml.title: GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark for NLU
aiml.text: GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark for NLU. GLUE includes 9 sentence or sentence-pair tasks covering NLI, similarity, sentiment, QA, and linguistic acceptability. Human baseline is 87.1. BERT achieves 80.4 while GPT achieves 72.8. GLUE motivates multi-task learning and general NLU models.

aiml.title: MMLU: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding
aiml.text: MMLU: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding. MMLU covers 57 subjects from STEM to humanities with 14K multiple choice questions. GPT-3 few-shot achieves 43.9% while expert human performance is around 89%. MMLU reveals that LLMs have large knowledge gaps in specialized domains.

aiml.title: IA3: Few-Shot PEFT is Better and Cheaper than ICL
aiml.text: IA3: Few-Shot PEFT is Better and Cheaper than ICL. IA3 rescales activations by learned vectors that are injected into attention and feedforward layers. IA3 adds only 0.01% additional parameters and outperforms full fine-tuning in few-shot settings while being more efficient than in-context learning at inference time.

aiml.title: Universal Sentence Encoder
aiml.text: Universal Sentence Encoder. Universal Sentence Encoder trains sentence encoders with a multi-task learning framework including NLI and response prediction. The transformer variant achieves stronger transfer performance on STS, SICK, and several classification tasks compared to averaging word embeddings.

aiml.title: StarCoder: May the Source Be With You!
aiml.text: StarCoder: May the Source Be With You!. StarCoder is a 15.5B parameter code LLM trained on 80+ programming languages from The Stack dataset. StarCoder achieves state-of-the-art on HumanEval, MBPP, and DS-1000, matching or outperforming GPT-3.5 on Python while being open-source.

aiml.title: kNN-LM: Nearest Neighbor Language Models
aiml.text: kNN-LM: Nearest Neighbor Language Models. kNN-LM interpolates a neural LM distribution with a nearest-neighbor distribution retrieved from a datastore of cached context-target pairs. kNN-LM improves perplexity across multiple domains without additional training and enables effective domain adaptation by swapping the datastore.

aiml.title: INSTRUCTOR: One Embedder Any Task
aiml.text: INSTRUCTOR: One Embedder Any Task. INSTRUCTOR generates task-specific embeddings by prepending task instructions to input text and training with a contrastive objective on 330 diverse tasks. INSTRUCTOR achieves state-of-the-art on MTEB without task-specific fine-tuning.

aiml.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
aiml.text: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization. Overoptimization of proxy reward models occurs as KL divergence from the initial policy increases. The gold reward first increases then decreases as optimization continues. Larger proxy reward models and larger initial policies are more robust to overoptimization.

aiml.title: A General Theoretical Paradigm to Understand Learning from Human Feedback
aiml.text: A General Theoretical Paradigm to Understand Learning from Human Feedback. This paper provides a unified theoretical view of RLHF and DPO as special cases of a general framework. Identity Preference Optimization IPO directly minimizes the KL-regularized objective without reward modeling and is more stable than DPO.

aiml.title: CRAG: Comprehensive RAG Benchmark
aiml.text: CRAG: Comprehensive RAG Benchmark. CRAG contains 4409 QA pairs spanning 5 domains with web search and knowledge graph APIs. The best RAG model achieves only 34% accuracy versus 89% for humans, showing that grounded generation remains a major challenge even with retrieval.

aiml.title: Lost in the Middle: How LLMs Use Long Contexts
aiml.text: Lost in the Middle: How LLMs Use Long Contexts. LLMs perform best when relevant information appears at the beginning or end of contexts but significantly worse when it appears in the middle. Performance degrades as context length increases. This motivates better retrieval to surface relevant information prominently.

aiml.title: Neural Approaches to Conversational Information Retrieval
aiml.text: Neural Approaches to Conversational Information Retrieval. This survey covers neural re-ranking from early learning-to-rank approaches to modern cross-encoder re-rankers. Cross-encoders consistently outperform bi-encoders for re-ranking but are slower. Two-stage retrieve-then-rerank pipelines balance efficiency and effectiveness.
